options.text: An IP leased by the DHCP for a host is permanent

answer.text: An IP leased by the DHCP for a host is permanent; DHCP assures connectivity ever users move from location to location
answer.explanation: A dynamic DHCP lease lasts for a specified interval and must be renewed; it is not a permanent assignment. DHCP can automate address configuration after moving, but connectivity also depends on a reachable server or relay, a suitable scope and a working network. The server selects addresses from its configured pool. Thus the permanence and guaranteed-connectivity claims are false, while pool selection and automatic acquisition are true.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A leased dynamic address is time-limited and can become reusable after expiration; it is not permanent.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: DHCP alone cannot assure connectivity after every location change; server, relay and network conditions matter.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A DHCP server manages an address scope/pool, supporting selection from a predetermined range.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Automatic acquisition of an address and options is a supported DHCP function.

evidence.quote: DHCP supplies addresses and configuration options. Typical initial IPv4 allocation is Discover→Offer→Request→ACK. The server manages its scope/pool, allocated leases, exclusions and reservations; options may include mask, gateway and DNS servers. A dynamic lease lasts for a specified interval, not forever.

Use a scope matching the subnet, exclude manually assigned server/router addresses, set correct options and provide a relay when client broadcasts must cross a router. Static assignments and DHCP can coexist; avoid address conflicts. DHCP lowers repetitive administration but availability/security depend on deployment and protection from rogue replies. It does not guarantee connectivity whenever a device changes location.

questions.hint: Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions.

University of Gondar model exam · Question 85

answer.text: Private IP address is used in the LAN
answer.explanation: Private IPv4 addresses are not directly routed as public Internet destinations. A gateway can translate those source addresses, often using port bindings so several clients share a public address. This works together with valid routing and the external connection. A missing default gateway must be repaired separately, and public addressing or uncertainty about the current configuration is not by itself a reason to enable NAT.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A missing gateway requires routing configuration; address translation is not a replacement for it.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Public addressing in a LAN does not automatically require address translation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Not knowing the address type calls for inspecting configuration, not blindly enabling NAT.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Private IPv4 clients commonly need source translation when reaching public destinations through this gateway.

evidence.quote: An IPv4 address is 32 bits; a CIDR prefix determines its network. Compute network=address AND mask; devices use a route/gateway for remote subnets. Private ranges are 10/8,172.16/12 and 192.168/16; private addresses are not directly Internet-routable. Neither IP alone nor a class label determines today’s subnet.

Routing selects a next hop using a destination prefix; NAT rewrites addresses. Many-to-one address-and-port translation (PAT/NAPT) maps internal flows to one public address using distinct port bindings. For example, two private client sockets can appear as public-address ports 40001 and 40002, with replies translated back to the correct clients.

NAT is often used when private IPv4 clients access public networks; it does not itself replace a gateway, route, firewall or authentication. One-to-one NAT and destination translation are other forms, so NAT does not always mean many hosts share one address. Public addressing inside a LAN does not automatically require NAT. Unsolicited inbound service access may require explicit mapping and filtering.

answer.text: Rebooting the system; Performing a software update; Resetting network configurations; Conducting a network scan
answer.explanation: Rebooting, updating software, resetting configuration and scanning can each help with an appropriate diagnosed problem. Change one relevant factor at a time when possible. A reboot can hide evidence and is not a diagnosis by itself.

Use bottom-up checks from physical link, top-down checks from application errors, or divide-and-conquer by testing a middle layer. questions.hint: Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 606

answer.explanation: Ping sends ICMP echo requests and checks the returned replies. Testing the gateway can help isolate whether the client can exchange IP traffic with that next-hop device. A VPN provides extended protected connectivity, FTP transfers files and DNS resolves names; none is the requested echo-probe utility. Missing replies need further investigation because filtering or loss can suppress otherwise reachable devices.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Ping generates the requested ICMP echo probes.

choices.explanation: A VPN provides protected connectivity rather than being an echo-test utility.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: FTP transfers files rather than issuing the specified reachability probe.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: DNS resolves names rather than sending ICMP echo requests.

evidence.quote: Ping uses ICMP echo messages to test IP reachability. A reply shows that the addressed host and path support that exchange; no reply alone does not prove the host is disconnected, because filtering or loss can suppress responses. Traceroute instead discovers responding intermediate hops through packet-lifetime expiry; it is a path-discovery diagnostic, not the same question as an end-to-end echo test.

DNS resolves names; DHCP supplies host configuration. SMTP sends/relays mail, while IMAP/POP retrieve it. FTP is a named file-transfer protocol; HTTP also transfers files, so “transfers files” is not an exclusive FTP description. HTTP/HTTPS serve web resources. SSH provides encrypted remote login; SFTP transfers files over SSH and differs from FTP or FTPS.

questions.stem: Which measures can provide a network security control under their ordinary stated purposes? Select all that apply.
questions.hint: Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 610

answer.text: Intrusion Detection System (IDS); User authentication; Data encryption; Network traffic analysis
answer.explanation: An IDS detects suspicious activity and alerts, while traffic analysis can provide additional detective evidence. User authentication establishes identity for subsequent access decisions. Correctly implemented encryption protects data against unauthorized disclosure. These mechanisms address different security needs, so all are examples of controls under the broad question. Their inclusion does not imply that any single mechanism provides complete security by itself.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: An IDS supplies detective monitoring and alerts about suspicious activity.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Authentication establishes an identity before access decisions and supports controlled admission.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Appropriate encryption protects transmitted content against unauthorized disclosure.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Traffic analysis can detect suspicious behavior and is explicitly included among security controls.

evidence.quote: An IDS detects/alerts; an IPS can block inline. Scanning identifies potential weaknesses rather than proving successful exploitation. A captured packet, open port or alert needs context. Monitoring network usage is not the same as configuring access control or encrypting communications.

Encryption provides confidentiality with correct key/nonce use; authenticated encryption adds integrity/authenticity. Unspecified encryption alone does not guarantee both properties. A password hash supports verification without recovering the original password; it is not a reversible credential store. Encryption can protect a recoverable credential only if its key is separately protected.

Segmentation separates groups of systems and enforces allowed flows with routing/filtering policies; VLAN membership alone does not establish complete security. NAC assesses device/user admission and can reject or quarantine unauthorized/noncompliant devices. Authentication proves an identity, while access rules decide which resources it may use.

questions.stem: In the note’s bottom-up connectivity procedure, which listed action belongs to the initial physical-link check?
questions.hint: Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 613

answer.explanation: A bottom-up procedure begins with power, cable or connector condition and link state before examining interfaces, addressing, routes or application policy. Checking physical cable connections directly fits that initial stage. Firewall configuration may become relevant later when evidence identifies filtering. Antivirus updates and backups serve maintenance or recovery purposes rather than the first physical-link inspection specified in this question.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Cable/connector and link-state checks directly diagnose physical connectivity problems.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Updating antivirus is maintenance rather than a direct connectivity-isolation technique supported by this stem.

choices.explanation: Firewall rules may require later inspection, but are not the initial physical-link check.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Backups support recovery but do not directly test or correct the network-connectivity path.

evidence.quote: Check power, cable/connector and link state, then NIC/driver state, VLAN membership, address/prefix, local gateway, route, DNS and finally application port/authentication. A recognized NIC makes a missing driver less likely, not proof of a working physical link. Ethernet commonly uses RJ45 connectors; an RJ11 telephone jack is not the expected Ethernet connection.

Divide-and-conquer narrows the working/failing boundary; it is not random trial-and-error. questions.stem: A script must recover a stored service credential to authenticate later. With the decryption key protected separately, which listed mechanism cryptographically protects that recoverable credential at rest?
questions.hint: Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 622

answer.explanation: The script needs the actual credential for later authentication, so a one-way password hash cannot meet the recoverability requirement. Encryption can protect the stored credential while allowing authorized decryption, provided the key is separately protected. Environment variables and configuration files describe storage or delivery choices and are not automatically encrypted. The explicit use case therefore identifies encryption without treating it as sufficient when its key is exposed.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Environment variables deliver or hold values but do not by themselves encrypt stored credentials.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Encryption protects a recoverable credential when its key is separately protected.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A one-way hash supports verification but cannot recover the service credential.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A configuration file is a storage choice and is not automatically cryptographically protected.

evidence.quote: Encryption provides confidentiality with correct key/nonce use; authenticated encryption adds integrity/authenticity. Unspecified encryption alone does not guarantee both properties. A password hash supports verification without recovering the original password; it is not a reversible credential store. Encryption can protect a recoverable credential only if its key is separately protected.

Keep reusable secrets out of source code and routine logs; obtain them from an appropriately protected credential service or restricted runtime source. Environment variables and configuration files are transport/storage choices, not automatic encryption. A script that must authenticate to another service often needs the actual credential/token, so replacing it with a one-way hash will not work. State whether the question is about password verification or recoverable service credentials.

answer.text: Log parsing; System calls; Performance counters
answer.explanation: Resource measurements can be recorded in logs, exposed through operating-system APIs or published as performance counters. Scripts may use any of those interfaces when the requested metrics are available. Signal handling instead reacts to process notifications and is not itself a CPU or memory measurement interface. questions.stem:
Suppose you are a network administrator and want to determine the path between two
connections, which often goes through multiple routers. Which command would you use?
questions.hint: Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 188

answer.explanation: Traceroute discovers responding hops toward a destination by causing packet-lifetime expiry at successive distances. It is therefore the appropriate command for investigating a multi-router path. Ping checks an end-to-end echo exchange and nslookup inspects DNS resolution, which do not supply the requested hop sequence. Some intermediate devices may not reply, so the displayed trace is evidence from responding hops rather than a guarantee that every router is visible.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Ping checks end-to-end reachability, not the requested hop sequence.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Nslookup queries DNS information, not intermediate router hops.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Traceroute discovers responding intermediate hops along the path.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The other commands do not all perform route-hop discovery.

evidence.quote: Ping uses ICMP echo messages to test IP reachability. A reply shows that the addressed host and path support that exchange; no reply alone does not prove the host is disconnected, because filtering or loss can suppress responses. Traceroute instead discovers responding intermediate hops through packet-lifetime expiry; it is a path-discovery diagnostic, not the same question as an end-to-end echo test.

netstat displays connections/endpoints/protocols and TCP states; netstat -ano displays numeric addresses/ports and PIDs. questions.stem: A data-center volume has exactly two equal disks and must retain service after either disk fails. One disk’s usable capacity is sufficient. Which listed RAID level meets these requirements?
questions.hint: Compare striping granularity, redundancy placement, usable capacity and required disk-failure tolerance.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 37

answer.explanation: With exactly two equal disks, RAID1 mirrors the data and leaves one disk’s usable capacity while tolerating either disk failing. RAID0 provides no disk-failure tolerance. RAID2 and RAID3 rely on different striping and redundancy layouts rather than the two-disk mirrored arrangement that meets these requirements. The choice follows the stated disk count, capacity and failure goal rather than the institution’s size or industry.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: RAID3 uses byte striping with dedicated parity, not the required two-disk fault-tolerant layout.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A two-disk RAID1 mirror provides one disk’s capacity and survives either disk failing.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: RAID2 uses bit striping and Hamming redundancy rather than the required two-disk solution.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: RAID0 cannot tolerate a disk failure.

evidence.quote: RAID0 stripes for capacity/throughput with no disk-failure tolerance. RAID1 mirrors; a two-disk mirror has one disk’s usable capacity and survives one disk failure. RAID2 uses bit striping/Hamming-code redundancy, RAID3 byte striping with dedicated parity, RAID4 block striping with dedicated parity and RAID5 block striping with distributed parity. RAID6 distributes dual parity and tolerates two disk failures. RAID10 stripes mirrored pairs; survival depends on which disks fail.

With N equal disks of capacity D, RAID0 usable=ND, paired RAID1/10≈ND/2, RAID5=(N−1)D and RAID6=(N−2)D. Hardware RAID may offload work to controller resources/cache but does not universally outperform software RAID. Rebuilds consume bandwidth; parity writes have overhead. A large university/bank alone does not select a level. Striping plus parity is not uniquely RAID5 unless distributed block parity is specified.

Which one of the following is WRONGLY stated about an importance of security 
policy?

sources: Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 85

answer.text: Passive system use is not a security-policy purpose
answer.explanation: NSA26 assigns policies risk reduction, coordinated required behavior and CIA goals. D’s passive-use statement does not describe those governance/protection purposes and is explicitly rejected here. B expresses the desired CIA objective, not a guarantee that policy alone prevents every incident. The remaining statements fit legitimate policy aims.

choices.explanation: Coordinating required behavior and enforcement across the organization is a legitimate policy purpose.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Passive use is not the defined purpose of security policy and does not express its governance/protection objectives.

evidence.quote: A security policy states required behavior, scope, accountable roles and enforcement. Begin with assets/service objectives, assess threats and weaknesses, choose controls, define exceptions/incident procedures, approve/communicate, monitor and periodically review. CIA means confidentiality, integrity and availability; neither sensitive-data protection nor availability alone is the universal primary goal.

A policy can require password controls, approved encryption, restricted administrative access, backups and patch deadlines; firewall rules implement part of it. Open unrestricted wireless access conflicts with controlled internal access unless intentionally isolated as a guest service. “Use the system passively” is not a purpose of security policy. Policies coordinate action and reduce risk; they do not guarantee every attack will fail.

blocks.text: Ping uses ICMP echo messages to test IP reachability. A reply shows that the addressed host and path support that exchange; no reply alone does not prove the host is disconnected, because filtering or loss can suppress responses. notes.title: Distinguish scripting features by their responsibility

blocks.text: Exception handling transfers control from a failing operation to a matching handler. A try block contains the attempted work; an except clause handles specified raised exceptions. A loop repeats operations, a conditional chooses an ordinary branch, and a function packages reusable work; these constructs do not by themselves intercept exceptions.

A module groups definitions and statements that can be imported. A class bundles data with functionality for its objects. These organize a program, while command-line parsing interprets the arguments and flags supplied at invocation. Their implementation can use functions or classes, but organization alone does not parse arguments.

A signal handler responds when a process receives a specified asynchronous event notification. Handling such a notification is distinct from reading CPU or memory measurements through an OS interface, a performance counter or a log that actually records the metric.
